review.reviewBody: I used to spend hours every week ordering food. Now it's simple, super easy, and I have free time to spend on other aspects of my restaurant.

@graph.name: Three steps, and no integration phase
@graph.description: There is no implementation project and no IT work to schedule to make this start. You send the lists, we create the logins, the orders begin arriving.

step.name: Send over your lists
step.text: A spreadsheet does it. Items and the price per account go into one admin screen, matched to the codes you already use.

step.name: Logins get created
step.text: We load each guide and set up the account, then the kitchen downloads the app. Most of them send something the same day.

step.name: The order arrives ready
step.text: The customer has approved it. It carries a number and the time it was sent, in the format your system takes.

@graph.name: Do we need an OrderEase alternative to take spoken orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. OrderEase manages what happens to orders after they reach you, from however many directions. VoiceOrder Solutions changes how one group of customers sends theirs to begin with. Keep the first and add the second; they work on separate parts of the same journey.

@graph.name: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than OrderEase?

acceptedAnswer.text: At getting a kitchen's order in already itemized and checked by the buyer, we think so. At reading an emailed purchase order, running your EDI partners or wiring up a marketplace, no: we do none of those. That job is theirs, and it can stay theirs.

@graph.name: We get a lot of emailed POs. Can you read those?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. We have no tool that reads documents, and we will not imply otherwise. We get accounts to stop sending documents, so the pile gets smaller instead of being processed. OrderEase's tools are built for the email orders that remain. One limit worth stating: only what comes through our app gets an order number, a timestamp or a stock update from us. A call or a voicemail does not.

@graph.name: Is OrderEase tied to VoiceOrder Solutions at all?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The two run apart, each with its own support, and neither has to be removed for the other to run. OrderEase keeps handling what reaches it, and our orders go into your system by their own route, in any format listed above.

@graph.name: Do accounts on the OrderEase portal have to move?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Buyers who like the portal keep using it. Our app is for the accounts that phone or email instead, and who gets it is your choice, account by account.

They are more open than we are here, and credit where it is due: their site publishes a starting figure and a setup fee, and says there is no free version and no trial. Ours is quote-based with nothing published, and since OrderEase stays, it covers only the step we add. Ask and we will quote you.

@graph.name: How fast could this be running?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most distributors have this working in 24 to 48 hours, and for most kitchens the first order follows the same day. Nothing in OrderEase gets connected or altered, so this asks much less of you than an OrderEase alternative that would replace it.

@graph.name: Where do the OrderEase details on this page come from?

acceptedAnswer.text: We took each OrderEase detail here from orderease.com, as published on 10 October 2026: their product and channel write-ups, the industry list and the pricing page. Their published results figures belong to them and are not quoted here. If something has shifted since, that is our error rather than theirs.
